items.prompt: A number, plus double the number, plus three times the number, makes 60. What is the number?
hints: Think of the number as 1 lot.
1 lot + 2 lots + 3 lots makes how many lots?
6 lots make 60. How much is 1 lot?
items.explanation: The number, its double and its triple make 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 lots of the number. 6 lots make 60, so the number is 10.

items.prompt: AB and BA are 2-digit numbers made from the digits A and B. AB + BA = 121. What is A + B?

options.why: If A + B = 8, then AB + BA = 88.
If A + B = 9, then AB + BA = 99.
If A + B = 10, then AB + BA = 110.
If A + B = 12, then AB + BA = 132.

hints: Try an example, like 29 + 92.
In AB + BA, the digit A is used once as tens and once as ones. So is B.
AB + BA is 11 lots of A plus 11 lots of B.

solution.say: Write the numbers using tens and ones.

items.prompt: Noor writes all the numbers from 1 to 20. Then she adds up every digit she wrote. What total does she get?

options.why: The tens digits of 10 to 19 add up to 10. Add them too.
Do not forget the number 20. Its digits add up to 2.
Add the digits, not the numbers. The numbers 1 to 19 add up to 190.
210 is the sum of the numbers 1 to 20, not their digits.

hints: Split the numbers into 1 to 9, 10 to 19, and 20.
The digits of 1 to 9 add up to 45.
Each number from 10 to 19 has a tens digit of 1 and a ones digit from 0 to 9.
items.explanation: The digits of 1 to 9 add up to 45, and the digits of 10 to 19 add up to 10 + 45 = 55. Adding 2 for the number 20 gives 45 + 55 + 2 = 102.

solution.say: Digits of 10 to 19: ten tens digits plus the ones digits.

options.why: Each 25 × 4 makes 100, and 100 × 100 is more than 1,000.

hints: Look for numbers that multiply to make 100.
Group the numbers in pairs: (25 × 4) × (25 × 4).

items.prompt: Mr Lim shares sweets with some children. If each child gets 4 sweets, 3 are left over. If each child gets 5 sweets, he is 4 sweets short. How many children are there?
hints: Compare the two ways of sharing.
Giving each child 1 more sweet uses up the 3 spare sweets and needs 4 more.
So 1 extra sweet for every child adds up to 3 + 4 sweets.
items.explanation: Going from 4 to 5 sweets each uses the 3 left over and needs 4 more, so 1 extra sweet for every child is 7 sweets. There are 7 children.

solution.say: Extra sweets needed for 1 more each.

items.prompt: Harga 3 buku tulis dan 2 pensil Rp21.000. Harga 1 buku tulis dan 2 pensil Rp11.000. Berapa harga 1 buku tulis?

head: Belanjaan
Harga
figure.alt: Tabel: 3 buku tulis dan 2 pensil harganya Rp21.000. 1 buku tulis dan 2 pensil harganya Rp11.000.

options.why: Kalau 1 buku Rp4.000, baris kedua menjadi Rp13.000, bukan Rp11.000.
Rp10.000 adalah harga 2 buku tulis, bukan 1.

hints: Bandingkan kedua belanjaan.
Bedanya hanya pada buku tulis. Pensilnya sama-sama 2.
Selisih harganya, Rp21.000 - Rp11.000, adalah harga 2 buku tulis.
items.explanation: Kedua belanjaan sama-sama punya 2 pensil. Bedanya 2 buku tulis, dan selisih harganya Rp10.000. Jadi 1 buku tulis Rp5.000.

hints: Look for pairs that make the same total.
How many pairs like that are there?
items.explanation: Pair the numbers from the ends: 1 + 19, 3 + 17, 5 + 15, 7 + 13, 9 + 11. Each pair makes 20, and there are 5 pairs, so the total is 100.

solution.say: The first 10 odd numbers add up to 10 × 10.

items.prompt: A number leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 2, by 3 or by 4. It can be divided exactly by 5. What is the smallest such number?
hints: A number that leaves 1 when divided by 2, 3 and 4 is 1 more than a multiple of all three.
The smallest number that 2, 3 and 4 all divide into is 12.
List the numbers that are 1 more than a multiple of 12, starting with 13.
items.explanation: The number is 1 more than a multiple of 12: 13, 25, 37, 49 and so on. The first of these that divides exactly by 5 is 25.

items.prompt: Today Ann is 8 years old and her mum is 35. In how many years will their ages add up to 63?
hints: Find the sum of their ages today.
Each year, the sum of their two ages goes up by 2.
The sum must grow from 43 to 63.
items.explanation: Today their ages add up to 8 + 35 = 43. Each year the sum grows by 2, and it must grow by 20, so it takes 10 years.

items.prompt: Fill in the magic square. Use the numbers 1 to 9 once each. Every row, every column and both long diagonals must add up to 15.
hints: Find a line that has only one empty box.
Add up the two numbers you can see. Then work out what makes 15.
Start with a line that has two numbers. Then use the new number in another line.
items.explanation: Every line adds up to 15. For example, the top row is 4 + 3 + 8 = 15.

items.prompt: Fill in the magic square. Use each of the numbers 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 once each. Every row, every column and both long diagonals must add up to 18.
hints: Find a line that has only one empty box.
Add up the two numbers you can see. Then work out what makes 18.
Start with a line that has two numbers. Then use the new number in another line.
items.explanation: Every line adds up to 18. For example, the top row is 5 + 10 + 3 = 18.

items.prompt: Fill in the magic square. Use each of the numbers 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18 once each. Every row, every column and both long diagonals must add up to 30.
hints: Find a line that has only one empty box.
Add up the two numbers you can see. Then work out what makes 30.
Start with a line that has two numbers. Then use the new number in another line.
items.explanation: Every line adds up to 30. For example, the top row is 16 + 2 + 12 = 30.
